t: You're on Lamb's Conduit Street, in Holborn. The name comes from Lamb's Conduit, a dam across a tributary of the River Fleet. It was paid for by William Lambe, a wealthy Tudor cloth merchant in the City who gave generously to good causes. He also funded St James' Church in Islington and Sutton Valence School. Traces of his conduit survive in a number of London street names, and this street is one of them.
